CausalChain: Fasting -> Energy stress in HCC cells -> Upregulation of miR-199a-5p -> Downregulation of HK2 and PKM2 -> Reduced aerobic glycolysis (Warburg effect) -> Increased reliance on OXPHOS -> Lower lactate production -> Less immunosuppression -> Enhanced sorafenib sensitivity
Hypothesis: Fasting induces upregulation of miR-199a-5p in HCC cells, which suppresses HK2 and PKM2 expression, thereby shifting tumor metabolism from aerobic glycolysis to oxidative phosphorylation. This metabolic reprogramming reduces lactate-mediated immune evasion and reverses sorafenib resistance in HCC.
Abstract: Recent studies underscore the pivotal role of aerobic glycolysis in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and drug resistance. We propose that fasting-induced metabolic stress may upregulate specific microRNAs, particularly miR-199a-5p, leading to the suppression of key glycolytic enzymes such as HK2 and PKM2. This suppression may shift HCC metabolism from a glycolytic to a more oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS)-dominant state, thereby reducing lactate production and its associated immunosuppressive microenvironment. Such a metabolic reprogramming could restore sensitivity to sorafenib and enhance anti-tumor immune responses. This hypothesis not only links fasting and miRNA regulation to metabolic changes in HCC but also offers a novel therapeutic angle to overcome drug resistance.
